title: Adaptive Log Zipper: tenant-aware compacting and deterministic ordering for high-throughput Loki/ELK ingest
creator: Ava Moreno
description:
Problem: During traffic spikes we observe high cardinality, redundant structured log lines (identical JSON structures with small variable fields) causing increased storage and downstream query latency in Loki/ELK. Existing ingest path performs light dedup and schema enforcement but relies on downstream compaction which is costly and results in higher write amplification and query tail latencies.

Goal: Implement an upstream "Adaptive Log Zipper" component in the ingest pipeline that: (1) groups and compacts similar structured log events into batched records while preserving deterministically orderable correlation ids and sequence anchors, (2) is tenant-aware (no cross-tenant mixing), (3) emits metadata to reconstruct original events for audit/debugging, and (4) integrates with existing Loki/ELK shippers without changing client formats.

Key capabilities and constraints:
- Similarity heuristic: configurable fingerprint on schema + stable key fields (service, trace_id, event_type) and a TTL window for zippering (default 250ms).
- Deterministic ordering: zipper assigns per-tenant monotonic batch anchors so reassembly retains causal ordering for trace linking and tail queries.
- Backpressure & SLOs: zipper must expose admission signals to the edge gateway; fall back to passthrough if queue/backlog exceeds threshold.
- Auditability: for zipped batches, store a compact manifest (SHA256 of original concatenated item ids, count, per-item offsets) in an index topic for rehydration. Manifest links must be queryable by trace/correlation id in Console.
- Privacy/compliance: support tenant-specific PII redaction policies during compaction; do not retain raw payload beyond configured retention windows for zipped manifests.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end pipeline shows >=25% reduction in write size for high-cardinality burst workloads in perf benchmark (simulated 50k rps multi-tenant burst).
- No increased 99th percentile ingest latency beyond 20ms for non-zipped requests; zippering should not inflate critical path for low-throughput tenants.
- Correlation ID joins across traces and logs still succeed at parity with current baseline in 95th percentile of test runs.
- Console dashboard updated with zipper metrics (zips/sec, average batch size, failover count) and an index view to locate batch manifests.
- Integration tests and a canary rollout plan defined.

Rollout plan:
1) Build zipper as an opt-in module behind feature flag and tenant policy.
2) Deploy to staging ingest cluster and run synthetic bursts and replay of production sampled traces.
3) Canary with non-critical tenants (1% of tenancy) with feature flag enabled. Monitor: zipper_failover, zipped_batch_size, manifest_write_errors, end-to-end tail latency from edge to Loki.
4) Expand to 10%/50%/100% with automated rollback on safety thresholds.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- We avoid changing client SDKs; all work is service-side. This reduces adoption friction but increases server-side complexity.
- Heuristic-based compaction risks under- or over-zipping; initial conservative defaults and telemetry-driven tuning expected.
- Storing manifests increases index writes; to limit cost we use a compact protobuf manifest and time-limited retention.
- Deterministic ordering is implemented with a per-tenant monotonic anchor plus per-batch ordinal; this trades off slightly higher metadata for simpler reassembly semantics.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for zipper heuristics and rehydration.
- Load tests: replay production logs with injected bursts; compare storage, per-token cost, and Lokistore query latencies.
- QA: tool to rehydrate zipped batches and verify event-by-event equality for a sampled set.

Migration and compatibility:
- Zipper is additive and opt-in; no mandatory migration for tenants.
- Provide a utility for one-off backfills: batch unzip and reindex into Loki for tenants that prefer raw ingestion.

Risks:
- Manifest index write failures could cause loss of reassembly ability; mitigation: synchronous manifest replication to a durable topic with retry and alerting.
- Mis-tuned heuristics could increase CPU usage; provide per-tenant knobs and auto-tune mode in later iterations.

Observability and dashboards:
- New Grafana panels under "Ingest / Zipper": zipped_bytes_delta, zipped_count, average_batch_size, zipper_latency_p50/p95/p99, failover_rate.
- Console query link: from a trace or correlation id, surface all associated zipper manifests and allow rehydrate playback.

Security & compliance:
- security_review_required: true. PII redaction policy must be enforced pre-zip. ACLs for manifest lookup controlled by tenant RBAC.
